subject: OrionBank — region pinning & data residency follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Claire O'Sullivan <claire@orionbank.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@orionbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Region pinning & data residency (post-call recap)

Hi Claire — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope the next steps: 

Recap (from our call)
- OrionBank wants to ensure PII and sensitive inference data remains in EU regions by default, with the ability to fail over to a secondary region only under exceptional conditions.
- Key asks: region pinning per-customer, cross-region failover policy, backups location, and logging/audit controls.

A few clarification questions for your security team so we scope technical options: 
1) When you say "remain in EU", do you require: (a) data at rest + model KV caches to never leave EU, or (b) only customer input/output and persisted artifacts (e.g., logs/archives)?
2) For failover: do you need automatic cross-region failover (hot standby) OR manual failover with an approval step (we can support both with different architectures)?
3) Backups: are backups allowed to be stored in a different region (e.g., for DR), or must backups also be EU-only?

Next steps I propose:
- If OK, Marissa (cc'd) will prepare a short architecture note showing Redwood Dedicated vs Private for region pinning and expected RTO/RPO tradeoffs.
- I'll attach our region-pinning whitepaper and a short SOC2 summary for initial review (attached).
- Could we schedule a joint call with your security lead + our SRE next week? Suggested slots: Wed/Thu 10–12 CET.

Thanks — I'll wait for Claire/Raj to confirm the three answers above and which slot works best.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Attachments: region-pinning-whitepaper.pdf

From: Claire O'Sullivan <claire@orionbank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@orionbank.com>, OrionBank Security <security@orionbank.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Region pinning & data residency (post-call recap)

Thanks Aditya — appreciated. Quick answers from our side (security + infra):

1) Data residency scope: We need both customer inputs/outputs and any persisted model artifacts or caches that could contain PII to remain in EU (so option a). Ephemeral compute in other regions is okay only if KV caches are flushed and not persisted outside EU.
2) Failover: We prefer a manual failover with documented runbook + approval (automated only for extreme full-region outage scenarios).
3) Backups: Backups of persistent storage must remain in the EU. We can consider copies to a restricted DR partner region, but only if encrypted with customer-managed keys and with explicit legal approval.

Also: what logging granularity do you expose? We need redaction options for PII in request logs and a way to disable raw request retention by default.

Happy to do the security + infra call — Wed 19 May at 11:00 CET works for Raj and me. Adding Security to this thread for visibility.

Best,
Claire O'Sullivan
Director, Cloud Security | OrionBank
claire@orionbank.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Claire O'Sullivan <claire@orionbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@orionbank.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Region pinning & data residency (post-call recap)

Claire — great notes, this helps a lot. TL;DR: we can meet those constraints; details below and looping in Laura (SRE) + Marissa (solutions) to map the architecture.

- Residual PII & KV caches: We can configure per-customer region pinning so that model KV caches and persistent artifacts are created only in an EU region (we'll persist to EU-only storage endpoints). Ephemeral compute can run in other regions only if you opt into cross-region compute; by default we enforce EU-only execution for pinned customers.

- Failover policy: We support both manual failover and an automated global failover policy. Per your preference we can implement manual failover with an orchestration approval step; we also support a "disaster auto-failover" mode that only triggers if the entire region is unreachable for N minutes (configurable).

- Backups: We can keep snapshots & backups EU-only. If you want DR copies to a non-EU partner region, we require CMK (customer-managed keys) and legal approval; we will document encryption controls and KMS configs in the architecture note.

- Logging/retention: We offer request-level audit logs, with configurable retention and redaction rules. By default, request payloads are not stored longer than 30 days for pinned customers and can be disabled; redaction hooks can be applied to strip PII before logs are persisted. I'll ask Laura to add the exact field/column names and retention options.

Attaching our SOC2 summary and a proposed multipoint MOP (workbook) for the runbook.

Proposed joint call: Wed 19 May 11:00 CET — Marissa and Laura can join.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, proposed-multipoint-mop.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@orionbank.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: OrionBank region pinning — architecture & actions

Hi Claire / Raj — thanks for confirming details and for the call slot. Quick action plan from our side and what we'll cover on the call: 

1) Architecture note (deliverable, owner: Marissa) — a 2–3 page doc mapping Dedicated vs Private options for OrionBank with diagrams for region pinning, KV cache flow, and backup locations. Will include KMS/CMK considerations. Target: EOD Mon 24 May.

2) Runbook & MOP (owner: Laura) — proposed manual failover steps, approval flow, and DR checklist. We'll include the multipoint MOP workbook and a sample playbook. Target: Wed 26 May.

3) Logging & retention matrix (owner: Laura) — exact retention windows, redaction hooks, and how to disable raw request retention for pinned customers. Target: Wed 26 May.

4) Security call (participants: Claire, Raj, OrionBank Security, Laura (SRE), Marissa (Solutions), Aditya) — Wed 19 May 2027 at 11:00 CET. Agenda: confirm EU-only persistence, walk runbook options, discuss CMK for DR, review logging redaction options.

Questions for you ahead of the call (if you can share):
- Any legal constraints on specific EU countries for backup storage? (e.g., must be inside Germany only).
- Do you have a preferred KMS provider (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or an HSM partner)?

I'll bring the architecture note and SOC2 summary to the call. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
